recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the approved FHIR-23035 narrative clarification without changing examples or adding new conformance mechanics; any future machine-checkable invariant around resolve() and targetProfile availability should be handled as a separate work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-23035 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for the FHIR-core StructureDefinition profiling documentation. It asked the Discriminator section to explain that elements appearing after resolve() in a slicing discriminator path are evaluated in the referenced targetProfile and that fixed value or pattern constraints must be declared there; the approved resolution also explicitly called for explaining multiple targetProfile behavior.
initial_application: The historical application commit 97dac7c066ececda81f3d3176017fb0f307e6ad4 added the main resolve() note to source/profiling.html for R5. Current source still only referred to an applicable singular targetProfile and did not explain the multiple-targetProfile case recorded in Jira and FHIR-I minutes.
additional_context: source/profiling.html is an active narrative page referenced from source/hierarchy.xml. ElementDefinition.type.targetProfile is repeatable and requires target content to conform to at least one listed profile. Later implementer discussion confirms that resolve().property discriminators rely on the applicable targetProfile to locate the fixed value, pattern, or required value set used for the discriminator, while profile authors remain responsible for slice uniqueness. No later final Jira or community evidence was found that reverses the FHIR-23035 disposition.
reconciliation: Updated source/profiling.html to say that, when a reference element lists multiple targetProfile values, the discriminator is evaluated against the targetProfile(s) that apply to the resolved resource. The added text explains that discriminator constraints may live in different target profiles for different target resources and that discriminator values must remain unique and non-overlapping across slices. A nearby misspelling of discriminator was also corrected.
source_changes: source/profiling.html: clarified multiple targetProfile behavior in the resolve() discriminator note and corrected a nearby typo.
